recognize_zh: 纖維性管壁中的一條小血管腔內擠滿大型異型細胞，核大、染色質空泡狀、核仁清楚，與紅血球混在管腔內，周圍間質內則無類似腫瘤細胞浸潤，符合血管內大 B 細胞淋巴瘤。
features: Small vessel within a fibrous wall whose lumen is filled with large atypical lymphoid cells
Large cells with enlarged round-to-oval vesicular nuclei and distinct nucleoli
Tumor cells admixed with intraluminal red blood cells
Surrounding fibrous stroma largely free of tumor cells
Adjacent empty larger lumen at the top right
describe_en: Section of a fibrous wall shows a small intramural vessel whose lumen is distended by large atypical lymphoid cells with vesicular nuclei and prominent nucleoli, admixed with erythrocytes. Similar cells are also present in nearby small capillaries, while the surrounding stroma lacks a significant extravascular infiltrate. No mass-forming lesion is seen in this field. Findings are consistent with intravascular large B-cell lymphoma; immunostaining for CD20 and an endothelial marker (CD34 or CD31) would confirm the intraluminal B-cell population.

ddx.vs: The intravascular NK/T variant is CD3epsilon+ CD56+ EBER+ and CD20-, requiring immunostaining to separate from the B-cell type.
Leukostasis shows circulating blasts or CLL cells with a corresponding peripheral blood leukocytosis rather than large atypical B cells confined to small vessels.
Metastatic emboli are cohesive clusters with epithelial or melanocytic markers rather than discohesive CD45+ CD20+ cells.
Reactive endothelial or histiocytic cells are bland, CD31+ or CD68+, and lack the large vesicular nuclei with nucleoli of lymphoma cells.
